title: Great time for Indian Markets? (after Trump's loss) | Akshat Shrivastava
creator: Akshat Shrivastava
source_note: Detailed summary generated from the video's English auto-captions; the video treats Donald Trump's election loss (Democrats taking the House) as the news event and builds its market view on it.
summary: Akshat Shrivastava reacts to Donald Trump's election loss - the Democrats taking the House - and what it means for US and Indian markets over the next three to six months. His core argument is that split power in Washington cuts market volatility: Trump can still make dramatic announcements, but with budgetary power now with the Democrats he has less ability to act on them, so markets face a more certain environment. He does not expect the AI bubble to burst, arguing AI backers such as Peter Thiel and Elon Musk have bipartisan support, though cheap, fast debt issuance will get harder. On the US market, he says the roughly 10% QQQ correction already priced in the expected Republican loss, with the index touching its 200-day moving average, and he expects QQQ to trade between 640 and 750 over the next three to six months - a consolidation to swing-trade or write puts against. On India, Nifty 50 rose 6-6.5% in the same week the US fell, but he still calls India a trading market, not a structurally investable one, until dollar-term EPS growth reaches 15% plus; resistance sits at 26,500 and he is exiting part of his own Nifty swing trade. His clearest call is Google: down about 30% from its peak at a 19 PE with 20% plus earnings growth over 20 years, and he is buying another major round and will keep adding, while cutting some Indian equities to move more money into AI stocks.
